## Current head verification — 2026-11-17

Current source **b8439609b60e2b9a20f6abadba7f63b7a907951d**: post-registration CONNECT ACK is linearized with per-scope teardown using a nonblocking send. Two regression tests cover the stop-between-registration-and-ACK race plus live ACK/timeout restoration. After a first Ruff format failure on `6d3d34c`, a formatting-only correction landed as `b8439609`.

**Exact-head hosted validation completed:** [CI #44031156340](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/actions/runs/44031156340) **SUCCESS, 14/14 jobs** (Ubuntu/Windows, Python 3.11/3.14, full tests, focused lifecycle, Ruff, mypy, installs/build and quota legs). [CodeQL #44031156434](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/actions/runs/44031156434) **SUCCESS, 1/1 job**. This is hosted validation of that source, not local execution; worker-local tests/lint/type/build remain **NOT_RUN** (per #675). Independent APPROVED review: **0**. Unexplained historical Windows `0xc0000008` remains separate in #679; DNS/connect cancellation limitations remain explicit. **Ready for independent exact-head review, NOT authorized for merge or release**.

Accepted CONNECT clients and in-flight upstream connections could outlive their acquisition scope because sockets were registered only after upstream connection completed. [Original receiving source](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/blob/9e7341986217fdca02a101d225ba4354bfe6480c/src/hungry_crab/fetch/acquisition.py#L280-L359).

The relay now owns clients before handler dispatch, uses a separate stopped registry per scope, refuses late upstream registration before acknowledgement, and retains ownership until sockets are actually closed. Teardown closes sockets without waiting for a blocked byte-reader lock; reusing the budget cannot revive an old handler. Shared download accounting and existing connection timeouts are preserved.

The owned test listener also shuts down and joins in a finally path before its listening socket closes. This repairs unsafe fixture unwinding on assertion failures. It does **not** establish the root cause of the historical managed-local Windows exception 0xc0000008; that forensic limitation remains open under #679. DNS/connect calls retain their existing cancellation limits; no hard DNS deadline is claimed.

## Exact-head hosted validation

Source **1785044d5cd787c693410420a7c04079964d4815**: [CI](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/actions/runs/43821116701) **completed success, 14/14 jobs**; [CodeQL](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/actions/runs/43821116617) **completed success, 1/1 job**. Native job results and full-suite summary logs were read back for this exact source, not inherited from earlier commits.

| Full suite | Passed | Skipped |

| Ubuntu / Python 3.11 | 5109 | 44 |
| Ubuntu / Python 3.14 | 5110 | 43 |
| Windows / Python 3.11 | 5145 | 8 |
| Windows / Python 3.14 | 5146 | 7 |

All four focused lifecycle legs passed **23 tests each**, covering partial CONNECT, normal/cancelled teardown, late completion, scope reuse, blocked-reader cancellation and fixture assertion unwinding. Ruff/format/strict mypy, supply-chain/build/sdist, base and clean installations, both real acquisition-quota jobs, B1/ranking and self-digest checks passed. Long full-suite jobs now depend on lint/type success, retaining all checks while avoiding full runs on an early style/type failure. Earlier failed runs remain failed in Actions.

Local pytest/Ruff/mypy/build: **NOT_RUN**, as requested. No paid model call, donor execution/acquisition, merge, tag or release.

Independent review has **not** been performed. Keep this PR **DRAFT/unmerged**, with #678/#679 open pending their actual review/integration and remaining diagnosis acceptance. This is the first P0 implementation slice of #675, not completion of 0.6.11.

## Active 0.6.11 implementation scope — 2026-11-16

Parent #675; package **T1**, priority **P0**. Route, early strict admission and per-operation authorization; retain PR #677.
Canonical [owner-approved specification](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/blob/5e79664/docs/releases/0.6.11-workflow-patch-scope.md). The owner now authorizes implementation and **checks in GitHub Actions only**. No new paid model/qualification run, donor execution or local donor download. No default-branch merge, tag or release is implied. Existing findings, acceptance and original failures below remain in force; work is not marked complete by this update.

<!-- workflow-audit-2026-11-14:fixed-pair -->

## Observed problem

The owner supplied an exact prey/maw pair, but the invoked eat workflow still initialized a discovery queue and leased a repository-search action. Actual host model usage was unavailable, so the controller stopped with `usage-unavailable`; analysis then continued separately through explore. The result was useful partial research, not a completed controller cycle. Unknown model usage was not zero.

The [eat protocol](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/blob/9942f2f4715d2e58180eaac608390421930b28c2/skills/eat/SKILL.md#L19) makes the metered route mandatory; [usage settlement](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/blob/9942f2f4715d2e58180eaac608390421930b28c2/src/hungry_crab/discovery_session.py#L397) correctly refuses to turn unknown spend into a qualified budget. Reuse that safety behavior.

## Bounded correction

- Select and freeze the execution route before semantic work: supervised fixed-pair research versus explicitly metered discovery/qualification.
- For an owner-selected pair, reuse sniff/compare, bounded index/inspection, receiving verification, novelty and local dry-run/delivery without inventing another donor search.
- Preflight host capabilities before leasing a strict metered session. If the owner requires actual model caps and the host cannot meter them, refuse before semantic spending.
- An ordinary explicitly supervised route may retain unknown model/currency cost, with bounded source/provider/time limits and no budget-compliance or qualification claim.
- Never stop a strict session and silently continue it through a second route. Preserve its unfinished state, charges and actual stop.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An already named pair does not issue repository-search requests merely to enter the workflow.
- [ ] Owned desktop-style controls with unavailable usage finish only the explicitly selected supervised route, reporting unknown usage.
- [ ] Strict-budget/qualification controls reject absent/invalid metering before a lease/model operation; known spend, overrun and interrupted reconciliation remain enforced.
- [ ] A stopped session grants no effects via route fallback; old sessions remain readable and unqualified where appropriate.
- [ ] Complete route, ordinary-present/held lead and original receiving verification are exercised on owned/exposed fixtures. Mechanical success is not measured usefulness.

Related: #533 (existing controller), #583 (host preflight), #541 (usage settlement), #540/#585 (unchanged comparative acceptance). This is an interactive fixed-pair admission repair, not a replacement controller.

This is an owner-requested planning issue from the 2026-11-14 fixed-pair audit. It authorizes no donor execution, paid campaign, merge or release. Preserve existing CLI determinism, source/license/origin guards, stable nutrient IDs and historical failed studies. #668/#669 fix the receiving Python miner; this issue fixes the workflow around that investigation.

issues/678.body:
<!-- release-scope:2026-11-16 -->

## Active 0.6.11 implementation scope — 2026-11-16

Parent #675; package **T6**, priority **P0**. Late relay admission/teardown; Windows crash diagnosis is separately #679.
Canonical [owner-approved specification](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/blob/5e79664/docs/releases/0.6.11-workflow-patch-scope.md). The owner now authorizes implementation and **checks in GitHub Actions only**. No new paid model/qualification run, donor execution or local donor download. No default-branch merge, tag or release is implied. Existing findings, acceptance and original failures below remain in force; work is not marked complete by this update.

## Problem

An acquisition relay handler can outlive the scope that owns it and enter forwarding after scope cleanup has already finished.

Source inspection of default branch `9e7341986217fdca02a101d225ba4354bfe6480c` shows this sequence in [`AcquisitionBudget._scope()` / `Relay.handle()`](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/blob/9e7341986217fdca02a101d225ba4354bfe6480c/src/hungry_crab/fetch/acquisition.py#L280-L359):

1. A request handler accepts a client and reads its CONNECT header.
2. It calls `socket.create_connection(..., timeout=30)`.
3. Only after both steps finish does it add the client and upstream sockets to `budget._sockets` (lines 303–305).
4. Scope cleanup stops the listener and closes only sockets currently in that registry (lines 350–359). The request handlers use `daemon_threads=True` and `block_on_close=False`; the explicit `thread.join()` joins the listener thread.

A client still sending its header, or a handler still connecting upstream, is therefore absent from the cleanup snapshot. There is no per-scope stopping state to prevent that handler from registering sockets later, acknowledging CONNECT, and forwarding.

**Evidence boundary:** this is a source-inferred race, not a runtime-confirmed reproduction. No donor code, tests, or reproducer was executed during the investigation.

## Why this matters

Normal completion or cancellation can return control while a relay request still owns live sockets. On normal exit, or cancellation that does not set a quota failure, the late handler can establish a tunnel and consume download allowance after the acquisition scope has ended.

This weakens the meaning of scope cleanup and releases the acquisition state lock before all relay activity has been excluded. It also complicates reuse of the same budget object: an old handler must not join a later scope.

This finding does not establish a bypass of the byte limit or filesystem quota. The specific defect is incomplete lifecycle ownership of accepted, pre-forwarding connections.

## Suggested bounded fix

- Give each `_scope()` invocation its own stopping state and connection registry, or an equivalent immutable scope identity captured by its handlers.
- Register accepted client sockets before any blocking header read.
- Coordinate registration and the transition to stopping under a lock. Once stopping begins, reject new registrations.
- If an upstream connection completes after stopping began, close it immediately without acknowledging CONNECT or entering forwarding.
- In cleanup, mark the scope as stopping and detach its registered sockets under the lock, then shut down and close the captured sockets outside that lock.
- Keep existing serialized byte reservation/accounting intact. Reusing a budget object must not reset a shared boolean in a way that revives an older handler.

Rejecting late results does not itself interrupt an already-running DNS/connect call. Keep the existing connect timeout, dispose of late connection results, and test or document the remaining cancellation limits. In particular, do not treat the socket connect timeout as a hard wall-clock bound on DNS resolution.

## Acceptance checks

Use owned local fixtures, fake connectors, and events/barriers to control ordering; no real GitHub/GitLab requests or donor execution.

- A client with a partial CONNECT header is disconnected when the scope exits, both normally and through cancellation.
- A fake upstream connection is held until cleanup finishes, then released. Its socket is closed, no CONNECT success response is sent, and no forwarding or download accounting follows.
- Start a second scope on the same budget object before releasing the first scope's delayed connection; the old handler remains rejected.
- Established connections still close on teardown, and the socket registry does not retain closed entries.
- Existing shared main/wiki download-limit, concurrent-accounting, process-cancellation, and cache-preservation tests continue to pass on Linux and Windows.
- Ruff and strict mypy pass.

## Existing work and overlap

[Closed #236](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/issues/236) established acquisition quotas and cancellation cleanup. This is a focused lifecycle follow-up.

The current [acquisition tests](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/blob/9e7341986217fdca02a101d225ba4354bfe6480c/tests/test_acquisition.py#L133-L256) cover shared stream limits, concurrent accounting, descendant cancellation, and preservation of previous cache contents. The inspected acquisition and transaction tests do not cover partial CONNECT headers or late connection completion during teardown.

At filing time, searches for relay and acquisition-shutdown issues found no matching task. Open PR #677 changes discovery admission and does not touch this component.

## Pykka reference and licensing

The adaptation was identified through direct inspection of Pykka at `9caec0e18e3bbf290de512752ffe91d489e2aad1`:

- [`ActorRef.is_alive()` / `tell()`](https://github.com/jodal/pykka/blob/9caec0e18e3bbf290de512752ffe91d489e2aad1/src/pykka/_ref.py#L67-L99) make stopped state explicit and reject work addressed to stopped actors.
- [`Actor._actor_loop_teardown()`](https://github.com/jodal/pykka/blob/9caec0e18e3bbf290de512752ffe91d489e2aad1/src/pykka/_actor.py#L279-L294) resolves pending requests with an explicit termination error.
- [`ActorRegistry.get_all()`](https://github.com/jodal/pykka/blob/9caec0e18e3bbf290de512752ffe91d489e2aad1/src/pykka/_registry.py#L60-L64) snapshots registered objects under lock.

These are lifecycle design references; Pykka's check-and-enqueue logic is not an atomic socket-admission implementation to transplant.

Pykka is [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/jodal/pykka/blob/9caec0e18e3bbf290de512752ffe91d489e2aad1/LICENSE). Prefer original code and synthetic tests implementing the lifecycle idea, without adding Pykka as a dependency. Copying or translating donor code/tests requires the applicable Apache license, notice retention, and modification markings.

This issue requests a focused fix and regression coverage; it does not authorize donor execution, an experiment harness, or unrelated actor infrastructure.


## Exact-head hosted verification — 2026-11-16

Implementation: [draft PR #687](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/pull/687), source `1785044d5cd787c693410420a7c04079964d4815`.
[CI](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/actions/runs/43821116701) completed **SUCCESS, 14/14 jobs**; [CodeQL](https://github.com/drevendev/HungryCrab/actions/runs/43821116617) completed **SUCCESS, 1/1 job**. All four lifecycle legs passed 23 tests each. Full suites: Ubuntu 3.11 5109 passed/44 skipped; Ubuntu 3.14 5110/43; Windows 3.11 5145/8; Windows 3.14 5146/7. Actual final-head jobs/logs were inspected.

The production relay fix owns accepted sockets through close and rejects late registrations; fixture listeners are stopped/joined on exception paths. No local checks or paid model run. No independent review, merge or release has happened. The historical managed-local 0xc0000008 diagnosis remains unconfirmed, so #679 and the broader release acceptance are **not** claimed complete. This issue remains open for actual scoped review/integration and any remaining acceptance.
